title: US strikes Iranian missile site on Qeshm Island after drones target Bahrain; Indian sailor missing
dek: Washington called the strike self-defence after the third Iranian attempt in five days to hit a US base. India condemned an attack on an LPG tanker in the Strait of Hormuz that left one of its 24 Indian crew missing.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
US fighter jets struck a Revolutionary Guards missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island, at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz, on Tuesday, a US official said, hours after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said its drones had hit a US radar at a Bahraini air base. The official said the strike, confirmed at about 1.08 am IST on Wednesday, was carried out "in self-defense" and was "in response to IRGC aggression targeting U.S. personnel and assets", according to reports. US Central Command said every Iranian drone launched at Bahrain had been intercepted and called the IRGC's claim of a hit "FALSE".

In New Delhi, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) condemned an attack on the Panama-flagged LPG tanker MT Tara Gas in the strait on 16 November. Of the 24 Indian nationals on board, 21 had been brought ashore at Khasab in Oman, two injured crew members were in hospital and one Indian national was missing, the ministry said on Tuesday evening. "The targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure must end," it said.

## What happened

The IRGC said early on Tuesday (about 2.19 pm IST) that its "combat drones" had carried out a "precision operation" against a US radar system at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, which hosts US forces. It said it was responding to repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones, according to reports.

US Central Command (CENTCOM) said in a post on X that "multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC today towards Bahrain were intercepted without any damage to U.S. equipment or injury to American personnel." Bahrain said its forces had intercepted and destroyed what it called "treacherous Iranian aerial attacks". US officials described it as Iran's third attempted strike on a US installation in five days, all of them intercepted, according to reports. Kuwait's military later said it was intercepting "hostile drone attacks"; it did not say where they came from.

Hours later, US aircraft used precision munitions against an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm, Iran's largest island, which sits across the main shipping lanes of the strait, according to the US official. Iranian media reported that an air-defence missile launcher in the Nariman area of the island had been hit, and the IRGC-linked Tasnim news agency said several projectiles struck the island. Ahmad Nafisi, a senior official in Hormozgan province, said the attack caused "no damage to residential, commercial, or infrastructural areas", according to reports. Iran's army also said it had shot down a US drone over the strait; the US has not commented on that claim, which could not be independently verified.

## The Indian crew of the Tara Gas

The MEA said the Indian embassy in Oman was monitoring the search and rescue operation with Omani authorities, and thanked the government of Oman for "timely assistance". It said "the continuing incidents of attacks on shipping in the region are deeply worrisome" and called for "free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through international waterways" to be restored as early as possible.

Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal had said earlier on Tuesday that all 24 Indian seafarers were safe, before a later update said one was missing, according to reports. Mr Sonowal said a second attack had forced the whole crew to abandon the vessel. The MEA did not say who attacked the ship, and The Declaration could not establish the cause independently.

It is the second attack involving Indian seafarers this month. On 10 November the Liberia-flagged supertanker MT Fujairah Energy, with six Indian crew, was hit by a projectile in the Gulf; four crew members were injured, one of them Indian, according to reports.

## What each side is saying

Iran's navy said on Tuesday that "the Strait of Hormuz is closed" and that safe passage required coordination with Iran, according to reports, and Iranian forces said three tankers had struck mines that day. The US says the southern shipping lanes have been cleared of mines, and President Donald Trump has accused Iran of exaggerating ship incidents to push up oil prices. None of Iran's mine claims has been confirmed by a shipowner, flag state or maritime monitor.

IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi accused Bahrain's government of cooperating in attacks on Iran, according to reports. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke to Bahrain's foreign minister, Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, condemned the attacks and reaffirmed US support for Bahrain's security, Bahrain's foreign ministry said. Saudi Arabia called for an immediate halt to Iranian attacks across the region, and Qatar called them a "serious escalation" while saying its mediation between Washington and Tehran was continuing.

Separately, Mr Trump warned on Tuesday that Iran would "pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before" if a reported plot involving a radiological "dirty bomb" proved real. Iran's foreign ministry rejected the report as baseless, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called it "RUBBISH", according to reports.

## Background

The US and Iran have been in open conflict since February, and the US has enforced a naval blockade of Iranian ports for months. Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war, has collapsed: tracking data compiled from the IMF's PortWatch showed two transits on 15 November, against about 85 a day before the crisis, according to reports. On 17 November Iran said a regional bloc had backed its two-day plan to reopen the strait, but Washington had not replied.

The strait matters directly to India, which buys a large share of its crude oil and LPG from Gulf producers, and has thousands of seafarers on ships in the region. India's wholesale inflation rose to 12.29% in October, driven by a 33% jump in fuel and power prices.

Brent crude fell about 0.5% to around $92 a barrel on Tuesday, according to reports, as the market weighed a supply surplus forecast against the attacks. Prices remain far above the roughly $72 a barrel seen in late February, before the war began. Iraq resumed pumping oil to Turkey on Tuesday at an initial 120,000 barrels a day, and Yemen's Houthis said they had hit Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline with drones, a claim Saudi Arabia had not confirmed, according to reports.

## What happens next

The search for the missing Indian seafarer continues off Oman. Mr Trump is due to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday, 19 November, on the sidelines of the APEC summit, and the Iran war is expected to be on the agenda, according to reports; a senior US official said Washington did not expect any agreement there.

## Timeline

- 10 November: MT Fujairah Energy, with six Indian crew, hit by a projectile in the Gulf
- 16 November: LPG tanker MT Tara Gas attacked in the Strait of Hormuz; 24 Indian crew on board
- 17 November, about 2.19 pm IST: IRGC says its drones hit a US radar in Bahrain; CENTCOM says all were intercepted
- 17 November, evening: MEA condemns the Tara Gas attack; one Indian missing
- 18 November, about 1.08 am IST: US official confirms strike on IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island
